title: Burning Steppes
body: The Burning Steppes were green country once, the northern reaches of the Redridge Mountains, until exiled Dark Iron dwarves raised their capital of Thaurissan here. When Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan called up Ragnaros the Firelord, mountains melted, Blackrock Mountain was born and the land was burned to ash. The sky still glows red above rivers of lava and charred earth. In the Second War the Horde made the mountain its stronghold, and at its foot Orgrim Doomhammer slew Anduin Lothar. Now the Blackrock orcs hold the steppes again, mining the hills for the metal of their weapons, and those who have seen inside their citadel say the clan answers to the black dragonflight, whose dragonkin swarm the eastern valleys. Firegut ogres guard Dreadmaul Rock for them, and Dark Iron agents prowl the ruins of the ancient city. Against all this stand only a few: the Alliance soldiers of Morgan's Vigil in the southeast, and an odd company of goblins, scholars and Horde fliers at Flame Crest.

title: Blackrock Pass
body: Blackrock Pass is the road by which most travelers from the lands of Stormwind reach the Burning Steppes, climbing north out of the Redridge Mountains past the Blackrock camp that watches its southern end. The change on crossing is abrupt. Behind lie green slopes and the lake country around Lakeshire; ahead the earth is black and cracked and the air shimmers with heat. Living fire haunts the pass itself. Flamekin spitters and sprites, small elementals of flame, drift among the rocks, lava crabs scuttle through the cinders, and an elemental of obsidian lumbers along the road toward Morgan's Vigil.

title: Morgan's Vigil
body: On a ridge in the southeastern corner of the steppes, a small company of the Alliance keeps watch from among the scarred ruins of an older town. Morgan's Vigil is the Alliance's only foothold in this land, and a modest one: an innkeeper, a weaponsmith and a dwarven gryphon master whose birds fly to Stormwind, Lakeshire and Thorium Point. Marshal Maxwell commands, joined by the night elf Helendis Riverhorn, the gnome mage Jalinda Sprig, the priestess Mayara Brightwing and the half-mad dwarf Oralius. Their fight is Lakeshire's fight too. The Blackrock clan the Vigil watches day and night is the same that crossed the mountains to raid Redridge, and dragonkin roam the valley to the north.

title: Dreadmaul Rock
body: Dreadmaul Rock is a great crag in the east of the steppes, riddled with caves and old mines and held by the Firegut ogres. They are allies of the Blackrock orcs, guarding the rock's rich mineral seams and keeping the clan's supply lines open. Ogre-mages and brutes crowd its slopes, and the hulking Hahk'Zor and Gorgon'och stalk among them. Something darker goes on in the caves. Reports of strange rituals among the ogres drew a Horde patrol here, and none of them came home. Fire elementals and lava crabs creep over the lower slopes, and the molten giant Volchan is sometimes seen wandering near its foot.

title: Terror Wing Path
body: North of Morgan's Vigil a long valley runs up the eastern edge of the steppes, and it belongs to the black dragonflight. Dragonspawn and wyrmkin patrol the Terror Wing Path in numbers, broodlings swarm underfoot, and black drakes prowl among them. Even seasoned travelers are warned not to come alone. Other hunters share the valley: venomtip scorpids, ember worgs and the great worg Deathmaw, Firegut ogres straying from Dreadmaul Rock, and malfunctioning war golems that lurch through the ash. At the valley's far northern end lies Slither Rock, the lair of the dragonspawn Cyrus Therepentous.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Terror_Wing_Path (eastern valley, black dragonflight whelps, dragonkin and drakes, advised not to go alone)

title: Slither Rock
body: In the far northeastern corner of the steppes, beyond the Terror Wing Path, a small cave opens in the rock. Few go there willingly. Slither Rock is the lair of a single great servant of the black dragonflight, the dragonspawn Cyrus Therepentous, and black broodlings scuttle near its mouth. Cyrus answers most visitors with contempt and a threat to devour them, yet those who prove themselves useful may leave with a bargain instead. For all his scorn, he will help a mortal against a foe they share, so long as it feeds his own hunger.

title: Flame Crest
body: Flame Crest is a rocky outcrop in the north of the steppes, reached by a crude bridge, with a small cave at its back. No kingdom rules it. Goblins and wandering scholars do business here: Tinkee Steamboil studies the local dragonkin, Kibler sells exotic pets from the cave, Yuka Screwspigot hunts for her worthless brother, and Maxwort Uberglint chases the lost treasures of the Dark Irons. The elven mage Mathredis Firestar seeks the librams scattered when the Scourge struck Quel'Thalas, and the drunken dwarf Ragged John wanders in from his jaunts to the Spire. The Horde keeps a foothold too, a wind rider master and a provisioner who serve its people in this hostile land.

title: Ruins of Thaurissan
body: In the heart of the steppes lie the broken streets of Thaurissan, once capital of the Dark Iron dwarves, destroyed when their sorcerer-thane called Ragnaros into the world. The Dark Irons have not given it up. Thaurissan spies, agents and firewalkers stalk the rubble beside iron war reavers, and a rare Dark Iron named Thauris Balgarr walks among them. Relics still lie in the ash. Touch one and a tormented voice may warn the intruder away as visions burn into the mind: eight dwarves at a ritual, a lone dwarf kneeling before a monolith of flame among seven corpses. Treasure hunters come regardless, drawn by rumors of a Tablet of the Seven.

title: The Pillar of Ash
body: South of the ruined city, out on the open plain, the Blackrock clan keeps the Pillar of Ash, one of its camps in the heart of the steppes. Slayers and soldiers stand guard, sorcerers and warlocks work their dark craft, and worgs bred in the Spire pace at their masters' heels. The orcs carry medallions of the clan, and those badges have become trophies: at Morgan's Vigil, the mad dwarf Oralius wants them by the fifty. Further west, more Blackrock camps dot the plain.

title: Blackrock Stronghold
body: In the north of the steppes, just outside Blackrock Spire, the Blackrock clan has raised a great fortress, hidden from the road but always watching for an Alliance attack. Battlemasters, slayers and warlocks man its walls, sentries and grunts of the Scarshield Legion stand among them, and the orc Gruklash, prone to fits of frenzy, prowls the grounds. The fortress shelters friends of the clan as well. Grark Lorkrub, who betrayed the Kargath Expeditionary Force to the Blackrock, waits here under their protection, sure that no enemy could slip into so heavily fortified a place to take him.

title: Blackrock Mountain
body: The northwestern sky of the steppes belongs to Blackrock Mountain, the volcano raised by Ragnaros's coming, and the road from the Steppes climbs straight to it. Dragonkin of the black flight hold its southern slopes, flamescale dragonspawn and wyrmkin among them, and great Blackrock drakes keep watch with them. Within the mountain the Dark Irons rule the depths and the Blackrock clan the Spire above, while orcs of the Scarshield Legion stand sentry on the slopes. Strange figures linger here. The ghost of Franclorn Forgewright, the dwarf who built the Spire, haunts his own tomb at its gate, and Lothos Riftwaker speaks of the rifts that tear the fabric of the world.

title: Altar of Storms
body: In the far west of the steppes, in the shadow of Blackrock Spire, stands the Altar of Storms, where Blackrock warlocks gather for strange rituals. They have unusual neighbors. Just beside the altar a human warlock, Mor'zul Bloodbringer, keeps a camp of his own, studying the place and perhaps hoping to harness its power. Warlocks of great skill seek him out, for he knows the rites that can bind a dreadsteed from the burning Plains of Xoroth, though the price is paid in blood, sweat and gold. His servant Gorzeeki Wildeyes, a gifted alchemist, prepares the ink and other trappings such work demands, and has a taste for spiders and beetles.

title: Draco'dar
body: Draco'dar is a stretch of scorched hills in the southwest of the steppes, crawling with servants of the black dragonflight. Flamescale broodlings tumble among the rocks, searscale drakes hunt the slopes, and the rare black drake Hematos is sometimes seen there, breathing fire on whatever moves. Giant ember worgs and firetail scorpids prowl the ash. Amid all this danger one man seems entirely at ease: Franklin the Friendly, who urges passers-by to ignore the lava and take in the joys of nature. Hunters who have challenged him tell a different story, for behind that smiling face waits the demon Klinfran the Crazed.

title: Marshal Maxwell
body: Marshal Maxwell commands the soldiers of Morgan's Vigil, Stormwind's only outpost in the Burning Steppes. The Vigil has paid dearly for its post. Its commanding officer, Marshal Windsor, was lost to a Blackrock raiding party, and a great store of intelligence on the clan went with him. Maxwell sees his war as one of two fronts: Stormwind fights the black dragonflight from within, and the Vigil carries the battle to its doorstep. He already knew the Blackrock were pawns of Nefarian, and with maps from a Horde spy he plans strikes on the Spire's war master, its ogre highlord and its overlord, then on General Drakkisath himself. None, he vows, will be spared.

title: Helendis Riverhorn
body: Helendis Riverhorn is a night elf who serves the Alliance at Morgan's Vigil, far from the forests of his people, and still asks the blessing of Cenarius on those he sends into danger. He has studied the enemy closely. The worgs the Blackrock orcs command never seem to dwindle, however many are slain, and his scouts have traced them to Blackrock Spire, where they are bred, trained and sent out to the clan. At the root of it, he has learned, is a corrupted she-worg the orcs call Halycon, a creature of dark magic. Like his comrades at the Vigil, he suspects the orcs themselves are pawns of the black dragonflight, which feeds their rage.

title: Oralius
body: Oralius is a dwarf soldier of Morgan's Vigil, and something in him has broken. He barks at every visitor as if at a raw recruit, cackles over his battle plans, and shouts, as a great confidence, that he is the only sane one left in the camp. His constant companion is Captain Winky, a friend no one else can see, with whom he argues, plots and on occasion trades a pirate's growl. He keeps a collection of severed ogre ears, and into one of them he calls out reports to some distant control. Mad or not, he wages his own war on the Firegut ogres and the Blackrock with deadly seriousness.

title: Mayara Brightwing
body: Mayara Brightwing is a priestess in the service of Count Remington Ridgewell of Stormwind's House of Nobles, who sent her to the Burning Steppes to scout the ruins of Thaurissan for treasures worthy of his family museum. Her search has led beyond the ruins, into Blackrock Spire. High in the citadel lies a chamber once called the Hall of Fortune, where the Dark Irons kept their relics, trophies and works of art, before it collapsed and fell to darker uses. Among its lost treasures is Doomrigger's Clasp, so encrusted with gems that it was said to make any dwarf who gazed upon it weep, and Mayara means to have it.

title: Ragged John
body: Ragged John is a dwarf of Flame Crest who is rarely, if ever, entirely sober. The soldiers of Morgan's Vigil remember that he was with their commander, Marshal Windsor, when a Blackrock raiding party fell upon them, and that he came back when Windsor did not. These days he makes his own jaunts into Blackrock Spire, where he has overheard the orcs speak of a poison they call Mother's Milk, after the great spider Mother Smolderweb. Ragged John wants a sample, still flowing in the veins of someone brave or foolish enough to be bitten. He swears it is not for poisoning anyone: it will make the best ale yet.

title: Cyrus Therepentous
body: Cyrus Therepentous is a black dragonspawn who keeps to his lair at Slither Rock and holds every mortal in contempt. Those who disturb him are left to wonder whether he will devour them whole. Yet he finds uses for lesser beings. His flight knows what was done in the Searing Gorge, and he will deal with anyone who carries a molt given by one of his kin, or who survives a fight with his minion. What Cyrus craves is the molten fire of Blackrock Mountain. He hungers for the inner flame of Bael'Gar, a giant born of the fires of Ragnaros in the depths below, and has altered the molt so that it can capture it.

title: Tinkee Steamboil
body: Tinkee Steamboil is a goblin scholar who has spent weeks at Flame Crest studying the dragonkin of the Burning Steppes. The land is dangerous, she admits, but scholars like her will do almost anything to advance their knowledge. Her inventions carry names as bold as her ambitions: the Draco Incarcinatrix 900, which draws the essence from a slain broodling, and the eggscilloscope, built to freeze a dragon's egg solid. She dreams of being the envy of dragon scholars around the world. Tinkee does not work for herself alone. Her research answers to a patron she calls her master, one she warns is not the sort anyone should wish to disappoint.

title: Kibler
body: Kibler is a goblin animal lover by inclination and a salesman by trade. From his cave at Flame Crest, crowded with cages, he tracks down exotic beasts for the rich and famous and tames them into proper pets, from worg pups taken out of Blackrock Spire to the spiders that hatch from its eggs. He pays others to take the risks. One of his hirelings was the goblin Bijou, who turned out to be a Horde operative spending Horde funds on his errands. His parrot Opus squawks his secrets to anyone who listens: that Bijou is lost, that dragons control the orcs, and that Kibler is under investigation by something called G.E.T.A.

title: The Firegut Offensive
body: Oralius of Morgan's Vigil has a plan, and it comes in three phases. The Firegut ogres of Dreadmaul Rock are allies of the Blackrock orcs, guarding the rock's rich minerals and keeping the clan's supply lines open, so the first blow must cripple their numbers: ogre-mages, ogres and brutes alike. The second must be decisive. Gor'tesh, the brute lord, rules the ogres not from Dreadmaul Rock but from a Blackrock structure to its west, and Oralius wants his fat head. The third is pure theater. Oralius mounts the head on a pike and sends it to be planted on the summit of Dreadmaul Rock, certain that the sight will send the cowardly ogres fleeing in mass hysteria. He speaks of a medal of bravery, then corrects himself: the soldier, of course, will be the one rewarded.

title: The Fate of Sha'ni Proudtusk
body: Sha'ni Proudtusk of the Kargath Expeditionary Force went into the Burning Steppes with her platoon to look into reports of strange rituals among the Firegut ogres. Three weeks later there was still no word. Warlord Goretooth told her husband, Thal'trak, to move on and attend to his duties, but Thal'trak could not leave his post at Kargath and could not let her go, and he begged for someone to search. Her remains were found at Dreadmaul Rock, and her spirit told the rest. The platoon had been captured and slain, and Sha'ni was saved for the ogre Krom'Grul's ritual, chained to an altar and tortured until she died. He tore her wedding nose-ring from her face and wore it on his finger. When the ring came back to Kargath, Thal'trak collapsed and would not take it. It was to have been her last mission before they made a home in the Hinterlands with her parents.

title: The Traitor of Kargath
body: Grandmaster Lexlort, head of the Kargath Expeditionary Force's reconnaissance, tracked one of the Horde's own across the Searing Gorge, through Blackrock Mountain and into the Burning Steppes. The traitor, Grark Lorkrub, had been caught red-handed passing word of the force's daily operations to the Blackrock orcs, and now sits in their great fortress believing himself safe. Lexlort's answer is a set of thorium shackles. Grark fights before he submits, and once bound he scorns his captor all the way, boasting of the power that comes from joining the legion of Blackrock and warning that his brethren will come for him. They do, again and again along the road through the mountain. If he reaches the Searing Gorge, Lexlort's men take him in hand, and the warlord prepares a final mission.

title: Eggs of the Black Flight
body: Tinkee Steamboil's study of the dragonkin began with broodlings. Her Draco Incarcinatrix 900 drew out their essence as they died, and the samples told her that dragon eggs might be frozen and preserved. For that she needed parts from her colleague Felnok Steelspring in distant Everlook, packed with the cold horns of chillwind chimaerae. With her eggscilloscope proven in the black dragons' rookery high in Blackrock Spire, and a collectronic module to carry off the frozen eggs, the harvest began. Then came a letter from one Leonid Barthalomew, saying that Tinkee's master Vectus wanted the eggs brought to Light's Hope Chapel. It was a trick. Leonid is of the Argent Dawn, and Vectus an undead mage of the Scourge in Scholomance. Had the eggs reached him, a great power would have fallen into the hands of the enemy.
